provenance_note: The isolated gateway served this repository's own copy of the app: capture.py's setup installed it from this checkout (POST /api/apps/install), trusted it and enabled it, and every picture shows its committed bundle (ui/dist/index.mjs) and backend. Kiro Crew still ships a built-in auto-improvement and refuses a second install under the same name, so the Kiro Crew tree the capture ran on is main 55439d8770 with only the built-in copy removed (src/kiro_crew/apps/builtins/auto_improvement and its BUILTIN_NAMES row); kirocrew_tree_dirty records that.
data_notes: The repository on screen is octocat/Hello-World, GitHub's own public sample repository (owned by GitHub's demo account, holding one README). It was connected through the app's own setup call (POST /api/apps/auto-improvement/setup-clone), which cloned it push-disabled into a throwaway scratch directory; no personal data is in it.

No improvement run was made: the sample repository has no tests, so a run would have nothing to check a fix against; the findings and pull-request lists are empty. The ruler card says not calibrated because nothing on the page calibrates it.
The ruler conversation came from a live model, so its wording differs from run to run.
